runs.title: create_agent

claims.text: The `create_agent` function generates a state graph that iteratively calls tools until a stopping condition is met.

citations.quote: Creates an agent graph that calls tools in a loop until a stopping condition is met.

claims.text: The function accepts a language model, tools (as a list, dictionary, or callable), and an optional system prompt for the L. M.

citations.quote:
model: The language model for the agent.
tools: A list of tools, `dict`, or `Callable`.

system_prompt: An optional system prompt for the LLM.

claims.text: The loop terminates when the language model's response contains no more `tool_calls`.

citations.quote:
The agent node calls the language model with the messages list (after applying the system prompt). If the resulting [`AIMessage`][langchain.messages.AIMessage]
contains `tool_calls`, the graph will then call the tools. The tools node executes
the tools and adds the responses to the messages list as
[`ToolMessage`][langchain.messages.ToolMessage] objects. The agent node then calls
the language model again. The process repeats until no more `tool_calls` are present
in the response.

sections.heading: Checkpointer for single vs. multiple threads

claims.text: The `checkpointer` persists state for a single thread (e.g., one conversation), while `store` persists data across multiple threads (e.g., multiple users).

citations.quote:

        Used for persisting the state of the graph (e.g., as chat memory) for a
        single thread (e.g., a single conversation).
    store: An optional store object.

        Used for persisting data across multiple threads (e.g., multiple
        conversations / users).
